title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 117 (Resolutions and agreements to be filed)

content.overview: Section 117 requires specified resolutions and agreements to be filed with the Registrar of Companies within thirty days, subject to the Act and applicable exemptions.
content.glance: Identify whether the resolution or agreement falls within section 117(3), then verify the thirty-day filing requirement, prescribed form and applicable exemptions.
content.study:
## Statutory framework

Section 117(1) generally requires a copy of each resolution or agreement covered by subsection (3), together with any explanatory statement required under section 102, to be filed with the Registrar of Companies within thirty days of passing or making it. Check the current prescribed form, electronic filing requirements, applicable fee and any exemption before filing.

## Resolutions and agreements covered

The statutory list includes special resolutions; resolutions agreed to by all members that would otherwise have required a special resolution; specified Board resolutions or agreements relating to powers under section 179(3); and the other resolutions and agreements expressly listed in section 117(3). Do not assume that every ordinary resolution or every Board decision must be filed under this section.

## Exceptions and consequences

Read section 117 with the provisos, rules and applicable Central Government notifications, including any exemption relevant to a company type. Failure to file may attract statutory penalties for the company and officers in default. Non-filing does not automatically mean that the resolution is void for every purpose; apply the statutory consequences to the facts and consider the position of persons dealing with the company.

## Practical filing checklist

Classify the resolution under section 117(3); determine the actual passing/making date; check whether section 102's statement accompanies it; verify the current form and exemptions; file within the prescribed period; retain the acknowledgement and filed copy.

sections.title: Scope of filing
content: Section 117 applies to the resolutions and agreements specified in subsection (3), not automatically to every company resolution.
Examples include special resolutions, certain unanimous member resolutions, specified section 179(3) Board matters and other listed statutory matters.

sections.title: Time and filing
content: The general period in section 117(1) is thirty days from passing or making the resolution or agreement.
Verify the current prescribed form, explanatory statement where applicable, fees and any exemption or notification.

sections.title: Consequences of default
content: Failure to file may attract the penalty stated in the applicable version of section 117.
Assess legal effect separately; non-filing should not be treated as automatically invalidating the resolution for every purpose.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: A properly incorporated company was challenged as indistinct from its controlling shareholder.
cases.issue: What is the legal effect of incorporation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A registered company is a legal person separate from its members, even when control and ownership are concentrated.
cases.holding: The company's separate personality was affirmed.
cases.relevance: Use for Companies Act s. 9 and corporate personality.

cases.name: Foss v. Harbottle
cases.facts: Shareholders sought relief for alleged wrongs to the company.
cases.issue: Who may sue for a wrong done to the company and when may exceptions apply?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The company is the proper plaintiff for corporate wrongs, subject to recognised exceptions such as fraud on the minority and ultra vires acts.
cases.holding: The proper-plaintiff and majority-rule principles were established.
cases.relevance: Use with oppression, mismanagement and class-action analysis.

cases.name: Needle Industries (India) Ltd. v. Needle Industries Newey (India) Holding Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court examined share issue powers and alleged oppression.
cases.issue: When does a corporate action become oppressive or invalid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court examines purpose, fairness, statutory power and resulting prejudice rather than treating every irregularity as oppression.
cases.holding: The corporate action was assessed under the statutory and equitable framework.
cases.relevance: Use for share allotment and oppression claims.

cases.name: Miheer H. Mafatlal v. Mafatlal Industries Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court reviewed a scheme of arrangement sanctioned by the company court.
cases.issue: What is the court's role in sanctioning a corporate scheme?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The court must ensure statutory compliance, class fairness, informed approval and absence of illegality, but does not substitute its commercial judgment for the company's decision.
cases.holding: The principles governing scheme sanction were stated.
cases.relevance: Use for corporate arrangements and tribunal scrutiny.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What resolutions must be filed under section 117?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 117(1) requires filing within thirty days of the resolutions and agreements specified in subsection (3), together with an explanatory statement under section 102 where applicable. The list includes special resolutions, certain unanimous member resolutions and specified Board matters under section 179(3), among others. Verify the current prescribed form, statutory exceptions and notifications before concluding that filing is required.
